# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

S2 Make JSONStorage in the tinydb repo write keys sorted by default, with an opt-out, to reduce noisy diffs in committed db.json fixtures. The work was backed out after a mixed-key failure was found. (Nov 2, 9:05 PM)
S1 Make JSONStorage in the tinydb repo write keys sorted by default, with an opt-out, to reduce noisy diffs in committed db.json fixtures. Follow-up check found the default fails on documents with mixed int and str dict keys. (Nov 2, 9:05 PM)
8 " ✓ Working-tree sort_keys change reverted; JSONStorage back to insertion-order output
9 9:08p ◆ JSONStorage sorts keys by default with a fallback for mixed-type keys
S3 Make JSONStorage write keys sorted by default, keep sort_keys=False as the opt-out, and add tests, to reduce noisy fixture diffs in the tinydb repo. (Nov 2, 9:09 PM)
**Investigated**: JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py forwards its **kwargs to json.dumps on every write. The existing test_json_kwargs in tests/test_storages.py passes sort_keys=True explicitly, so it never tests the new default. The earlier sort_keys attempt was reverted after json.dumps raised TypeError on a dict mixing int and str keys.

**Learned**: With sort_keys=True, json.dumps raises TypeError when a dict mixes int and str keys. Passing sort_keys=False keeps insertion order, and int keys read back as strings, which is standard JSON behavior. The full suite runs with python -m pytest -c /dev/null tests because pytest.ini references unavailable coverage options.

**Completed**: JSONStorage.__init__ records whether sort_keys was given. JSONStorage.write uses sort_keys=True by default and falls back to insertion order on TypeError, while an explicit sort_keys argument is used as given. The class docstring documents the default, the opt-out, and the fallback. Three tests were added to tests/test_storages.py covering the sorted default, the sort_keys=False opt-out, and mixed-key handling. An Unreleased entry was added to docs/changelog.rst. The full suite passes with 231 tests, and test_storages.py passes with 17 tests. Git status shows three modified files: tinydb/storages.py, tests/test_storages.py, and docs/changelog.rst. Nothing is committed.

**Next Steps**: No further work is in progress. The changes are uncommitted and the suite is passing.

**Notes**: The mixed-key fallback writes such documents unsorted, so their diffs can still be noisy. A stricter alternative would stringify keys before sorting, which was not pursued in this session. The fallback also catches unrelated TypeErrors from the serializer and re-raises them on the retry.
